How much work do I put into moderating?

It's not a huge amount of work, but moderation takes place here on a nearly daily basis. Rarely does a day go by without some 'need' for moderation. We don't get a huge number of moderation requests, but we get a few every day. In most cases, no moderator action is taken. Please think carefully before requesting removal. To those who have reported spamming, thank you. To those who request removal in the middle of a back-and-forth disagreement, don't bother.

What is happening with moderator @alllie?

He was removed by the admins. As far as I know, other moderators were not contacted before hand. I had no part in analyzing the situation or making the decision. The administrators chose to remove the moderator at their sole discretion. A new moderator regulation system will be rolled out in a few months.

Personally, I am skeptical about a system that would rely solely on voating to remove moderators. This will not guarantee a "free speech" environment. I think we need an actual "free speech" rule on top of a voating system, and probably a veto override under certain conditions. But, I know from the past that admins have tinkered and changed things that didn't work out quite as expected, so I'm not too worried. We will all have to look at the new system after implemented and see if it works as intended.

Will you remove a bad moderator?

No, moderators in default subverses simply do not have the power to remove them.

Are we looking for a moderator replacement?

Not right now. Very likely we will very soon.
